name: Three Gardens House
notes: Sheet 0 (AGi architects, Mubarak Al-Kabeer, Kuwait): from the street the house is a wall of pale cream limestone cladding pulled apart into stacked blocks, with a big square cut at the top holding a planted roof garden behind a perforated screen, an angled dark perforated-metal skin folding over the upper floor and roof (also the sun-roof and privacy screen), and a row of olive trees against the street wall. Inside it is organised round three gardens at three levels - the Wet Garden on the ground floor round a pool and fountains, the evening and summer gardens above, and a basement garden below street level with a long lap pool - and the court is open to the sky under the perforated roof (the third and last photographs). Modelled: the stacked limestone blocks, the street window and its planted ledge, the open court with its pool and white walls, the dark mesh roof planes and wall, the garden wall, garage, olives. Not modelled: the basement garden and lap pool, interior floors. Guessed: dimensions (a 28 x 26 m house of three storeys), which way the front faces. A private home placed at its region only (Kuwait); nothing here places it closer.
